stem.text: The function f is differentiable for all real numbers, and selected values of f are given in the table. Must there be a value c, with \( 1 < c < 8 \), for which \( f(c) = -4 \)? Justify your answer.

answer_key.label: Yes. Since f is differentiable, it is continuous on \( [3, 6] \), and \( f(3) = -7 < -4 < f(6) = 0 \), so the Intermediate Value Theorem gives at least one such c.

worked_solution.text: Because f is differentiable, f is continuous, in particular on \( [3, 6] \).
From the table, \( f(3) = -7 < -4 < f(6) = 0 \), so -4 lies between the values of f at the ends of \( [3, 6] \).
By the Intermediate Value Theorem there is at least one c with \( 3 < c < 6 \) and \( f(c) = -4 \), and that c also satisfies \( 1 < c < 8 \). So yes, such a c must exist.
